move: iPhone lock screen behind sliding fluted glass ribs, colours refract
how: A phone frame with Dynamic Island, clock, a glass notification and controls holds a 340x700 canvas. Each frame the canvas draws four coloured radial blobs orbiting on ellipses (1 or 2 cycles per D) into a source canvas, then redraws it column by column through a 22px sawtooth lens so every rib stretches and offsets the picture, adds a specular highlight and shadow edge per rib, and slides the rib pattern one full rib per D so it loops. A paused GSAP timeline turns the phone rotationY -14 to 14 and rotationX 4 to -4 in one sine yoyo cycle, and a notification drops in with expo.out at 0.16 D and lifts out with power3.in at 0.78 D. A violet halo glows behind.
adapt: Change the four blob colours and the base tint, the lock-screen time and date, the notification brand and message; rib width RIB controls the flute pitch. Keep the one-rib slide per D and integer blob orbits.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone DOM and both canvases; animate(el, shot, D) returns the phone/notification timeline with an added linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate redraws the source and the per-column refraction. The seek override that chains the DOM timeline onto fx.register is replaced by that single timeline; canvas size is fixed at 340x700 regardless of shot size.
caveats: per-column drawImage (340 calls) plus per-rib gradients every frame; fine at this size, slow if the canvas grows
backdrop-filter blur on the notification and controls
DOM motion and canvas motion are combined by overriding window.__fx.seek
